Research Experience

Monte Carlo Methods for Path-Dependent Convertible Bond Valuation

M.Phil. research · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen · 2023–2024
Advisor: Prof. Gongqiu Zhang

My master's research focused on the numerical valuation of convertible bonds with path-dependent contractual provisions, using Monte Carlo simulation, backward dynamic programming, and regression-based approximation.

  • Stochastic modeling. Simulated stock-price dynamics using geometric Brownian motion and modeled path-dependent call, put, and conversion-price reset provisions.
  • Numerical methods. Applied least-squares regression to approximate continuation values within a backward dynamic-programming framework.
  • Mathematical analysis. Studied the least-squares formulation and the full-column-rank condition for uniqueness of the regression coefficients.
  • Numerical experiments. Investigated how model assumptions, regression specifications, and contractual exercise rules affect valuation results.

Master's thesisPricing manuscript PDF

Related manuscript: Valuation Model of Chinese Convertible Bonds Based on Monte Carlo Simulation (arXiv:2409.06496; preprint). The full thesis also includes multi-factor strategy research.

Wavelet Frames and Numerical Optimization

Undergraduate thesis · Tongji University · Advisor: Jae Kyu Choi

Studied wavelet-frame regularization for reconstructing images from noisy, blurred, or incomplete observations. Building on existing models and algorithms, the thesis covered the following work.

  • Model relationships.Examined multiresolution analysis and tight wavelet frames, the connections between analysis-based, synthesis-based, and balanced reconstruction models, and the relationship between soft thresholding and sparse regularization.
  • Numerical solution.Derived variable-splitting and augmented-Lagrangian formulations for the analysis-based model and worked through ADMM / Split Bregman iterations, including FFT-based subproblem solution for deblurring and thresholding updates.
  • Convergence study.Examined the assumptions behind existing convergence results, distinguishing convergence of objective values from convergence of iterates when the solution is unique, and discussed computational complexity.
  • Numerical experiments.Compared B-spline and Haar wavelet-frame methods with total variation for deblurring and inpainting, using PSNR, HFEN, SSIM, iteration counts, and runtime to evaluate reconstruction quality and computational cost.

Thesis: Image Restoration: a Wavelet Frame Based Approach and Beyond
